lines.text: Over twenty thousand people signed up for this hackathon.
Somebody has to check all of that. That's you.
So I built something for you.
This is Hearsay. Write what your customers say. Hearsay plays it against your add-on, mishearings included, and fails the build when it would sound wrong.
Here's how it works. When someone talks to your add-on, Amazon turns the speech into text, and the assistant's model picks your tool. Only the next step is your code.

lines.text: So Hearsay plays those two parts from your test case. The customer says fifteen, your tool gets fifteen. And because speech recognition slips, it tries fifty too.

lines.text: Every finding cites the rule it breaks, and most are Amazon's published requirements for add-ons.
A tool answers within half a second. A reply stays under thirty seconds. No JSON read aloud. At most five options. And no payment without a question that names what and how much.

lines.text: Hearsay is unofficial, and it doesn't certify anything. It just tells you early.
Here's a grocery add-on, with Hearsay playing its customer.
Fifteen is heard as fifty, and the add-on just says: added. The customer says no, and the order changes anyway.

lines.text: Twenty errors. The pull request fails.
Same tests, fixed build. The customer grants a budget once, and money only moves after a yes.
You can reorder groceries up to forty dollars today.
Yes.
Add fifteen dollars of fruit.
That would go over the total budget you gave me. You can add less, or give me a bigger budget.
Add two cartons of milk.
Added two cartons of milk. Your cart is seven dollars and forty cents.
Place the order.
Place the order: two cartons of milk, seven dollars and forty cents?
No, not yet.
Okay, I did not place the order. Your cart is still there.
Zero errors. Green.
You don't even have to run it yourself. Hearsay is also an MCP server, so your coding agent runs it, fixes what it finds, and checks again until it's green.
And it can't cheat. Your suite is locked, and Hearsay keeps test cases your agent never sees.
We measured it.
A suite alone made agents stop at green. So Hearsay now shows what your suite doesn't cover.
Result: as good as a precise prompt on unseen cases, better on the rules nobody told the agent about, and zero defects left behind.
It runs in CI, without API keys, and fails the pull request before your customers ever hear it.
Hearsay is open source. Point it at your server.
